endpoint: `https://web-api.tp.entsoe.eu/api?securityToken=<token>&documentType=<code>&...` (GET; POST with XML StatusRequest also supported). Outage document types (from the user guide §4.7 / Appendix A.9, DOCS-ONLY): `A77` Production unit unavailability (Art. 15.1.C/D), `A78` Transmission infrastructure unavailability (Art. 10.1.A/B), `A80` Generation unit unavailability (Art. 15.1.A/B), `A53` Consumption unit unavailability (Art. 7.1.A/B), `A79` Offshore grid infrastructure unavailability; parameters `biddingZone_Domain`/`in_Domain`/`out_Domain` (EIC), `periodStart`/`periodEnd` (yyyyMMddHHmm), optional `docStatus`, `businessType` (A53 planned / A54 forced), `periodStartUpdate`/`periodEndUpdate`.
licence: Terms of Use (v. 29/03/2023, effective 01/11/2023) + "Open Data" list per clause 2.5: "ENTSO-E publishes the list of data which is open for free re-use with no need to seek the prior agreement of the respective Primary Owner of Data"; the list "incorporat[es] Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC-BY 4.0)" (18/02/2022 version). notes: Household value assessment: TSO-level unavailability (A77/A78/A80) is about generators and transmission lines, NOT distribution outages that hit households; it will not tell a family their street is dark. It is useful for (a) system-stress signals (large forced generation loss + tight margin), (b) day-ahead prices (A44) for cost-saving nudges, (c) scheduled interconnector/line outages as weak precursor. Real household outage info lives with DSOs (per-country files). Turkey (TEIAS) publishes only some data; not all 39 countries are in TP.
